parsed.study_design: Ecological spatial case study developing a composite vulnerability index using census-sector GIS analysis and supplementary social-media data
parsed.population_and_sample: Urban population of São José dos Campos, São Paulo; 871 census sectors, with supplementary analysis of more than 1,300 Facebook comments
parsed.exposure: A 2016 mining-dam failure that interrupted the municipal drinking-water supply, assessed across administrative regions and zoning/urbanization classes reflecting infrastructure availability, land-use planning, and irregular settlement conditions
parsed.outcome: Spatially distributed social vulnerability to drinking-water shortage and unequal access during supply interruption, measured by SUWSVI categories based on household income, female household headship, and child/elderly dependency
parsed.rationale: The Methods (§§2.1–2.2, pp. 176–180) identify the population, interruption of public drinking-water service, administrative and zoning context, census-sector sample, variables, and index-construction design. Results and Discussion (pp. 180–184) empirically relate vulnerability and reported shortages to administrative regions, infrastructure, zoning classes, irregular housing, and access to alternative public wells; the Conclusion states that the index mapped groups facing difficulty accessing water when public supply failed (p. 184).
